title: A morphism from a proper scheme to a separated scheme over the same base is proper
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $h:X\to S$ a proper morphism, $q:Y\to S$ a separated morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism with $q\circ f=h$. Then $f$ is proper; in particular it is universally closed and of finite type.

mathlib_searches.query: if g ∘ f is proper and g is separated then f is proper

mathlib_searches.results: Proper.lean:124 lemma IsProper.of_comp [IsProper (f ≫ g)] [IsSeparated g] : IsProper f

mathlib_match.how: exact: with g = q, f ≫ g = h (Mathlib composes left to right); the 'in particular' is the definition of IsProper (IsSeparated, UniversallyClosed, LocallyOfFiniteType, QuasiCompact)
